To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an analytical theory for the evolution of path instability of buoyancy-driven objects that is based on an exact set of amplitude equations with coefficients determined by the underlying linear problem and that we have shown, using both numerical simulations and experiments, that this theory is accurate in predicting the evolution of path stability of buoyancy-driven particles and air bubbles.

a weakly nonlinear model based on a set of two amplitude equations with exact, rather than approximate, coefficients accurately predicts the style, frequency, and maximum inclination angle of path oscillations of buoyancy-driven objects in a viscous liquid.

the weakly nonlinear model with the exact coefficients for the evolution of the amplitude of the first pair (i.e., the fundamental) of unstable modes is able to predict well the style and the characteristics (e.g. frequency and maximum inclination) of path oscillation in the case of the fluttering and helical paths of buoyancy-driven disks and air bubbles in a viscous fluid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical model for the evolution of the path of a buoyancy-driven body moving in a viscous fluid.
the study of the dynamics of a buoyant body moving in a slightly-viscous fluid.
the development and analysis of a generic weakly nonlinear model for the path instability of gravity- or buoyancy driven bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model presented here, which has exact coefficients, provides a good description of the evolution of path instabilities in buoyancy-driven bodies.
the model is able to predict the onset of instability and the style of motion for a large variety of buoyant bodies.
the model is able to capture most of the essential features of the evolution of path instabilities of buoyancy-driven particles in a viscous fluid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weakly nonlinear model with the exact coefficients can predict the characteristics and styles of the path oscillations of buoyancy-driven particles in a slightly viscously fluid.
the model is able to describe the path instability of buoyancy-driven objects, and the model is valid for the entire evolution process from the onset of path oscillation to the fully developed state.

the model is capable of predicting the onset and evolution of path oscillations in buoyancy-driven systems with a single pair of unstable modes and that this model is applicable to a wide range of systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a wide range of parameters and body shapes, the evolution of path oscillations is governed by a pair of coupled equations with coefficients that depend only on the body’s shape.
a simple, yet accurate, model can be obtained by a weakly nonlinear analysis that does not require a priori knowledge of the path style.
the weakly nonlinear theory provides a simple and accurate description of the path evolution of buoyancy-driven systems.
